proof: A randomized learner may emulate any deterministic learner. Theorem 3 of Filmus--Hanneke--Mehalel--Moran identifies the respective optimal $k$-realizable mistake bounds with the two dimensions, giving the inequality.
proof_source: Theorem 3 of \cite{filmus2023randomized}, together with deterministic learners as a subclass of randomized learners.
witness_verification: For the two complementary constant concepts, deterministic value is $2k+1$, whereas the randomized value is $k+(k+\tfrac12)\binom{2k}{k}4^{-k}=k+O(\sqrt{k})$. Hence their difference is unbounded as $k$ grows.
name: $k$-Mistake Littlestone Dimension / Randomized $k$-Mistake Littlestone Dimension
